question.text: <math> <mrow> <mn>2.68</mn><mo>×</mo><msup> <mrow> <mn>10</mn></mrow> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> moles of a solution containing an ion <math> <mrow> <msup> <mtext>A</mtext> <mrow> <mtext>n+</mtext></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> require <math> <mrow> <mtext>1</mtext><mtext>.61</mtext><mo>×</mo><msup> <mrow> <mtext>10</mtext></mrow> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> moles of  <math> <mrow> <msubsup> <mtext>MnO</mtext> <mn>4</mn> <mo>-</mo> </msubsup> </mrow> </math> ion for the oxidation of <math> <mrow> <msup> <mtext>A</mtext> <mrow> <mtext>n+</mtext></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> to <math> <mrow> <msubsup> <mtext>AO</mtext> <mn>3</mn> <mrow> <mo>-</mo> </mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> in acidic medium. What is the value of <math> <mrow> <mtext>n?</mtext></mrow> </math>

solution.text:
A n+ → A +5 O 3 − + 5−n   e −  × 5, Oxidation half reaction

MnO4-+8H++5e-→Mn2++4H2O × (5-n), Reduction half reaction

Applying reaction stoichiometry,

5 moles of An+ =  5-n moles of MnO 4-
5 5-n = 2.68 × 1 0 - 3 1.61 × 10 - 3 = 1.66 = 5 3
5 - n = 3
∴ n = 2
